notes:
### Improved
- Hotspots and weak Wi-Fi no longer break up the sound. Hotspots (a PC's
  Mobile Hotspot, a phone's hotspot) and Wi-Fi power saving hold packets for
  100–300 ms and then release them all at once; SYNQ now enlarges its buffer
  to ride through those stalls instead of cutting, and shrinks it again when
  the network calms down. The phone shows "Unstable network · +X ms buffer to
  avoid cuts" while this happens. On a steady network nothing changes.

### New
- Full-screen player on the phone in landscape: the status and navigation
  bars hide (swipe from the edge to show them).
- The phone's home screens use two columns in landscape.

### Fixed
- "Forget" on the PC now also removes the pairing: a forgotten phone has to
  pair again instead of reconnecting straight away. A pairing request brings
  SYNQ back from the tray.
- SYNQ Desktop no longer uses a full CPU core while hidden in the tray
  (about 12% before, under 1% now).

### Improved
- Lighter on the phone's battery: the media notification only updates when
  something changed, and the progress bar redraws a few times a second
  instead of every frame.
- Media apps on the PC are checked less often when nothing is shown.

### New
- Media controls in the phone's notification and on the lock screen: artwork,
  play/pause, previous/next and seeking for whatever plays on the computer
  (also from Bluetooth and headset buttons).
- Updates in the app: on every launch SYNQ checks for a new version and shows
  a dialog; "Update now" downloads, verifies and installs it (PC and phone).

### Improved
- The phone's player works in landscape: artwork with the seek bar on the
  left, controls on the right; it no longer gets stuck when rotating.
- "Check for updates" on the PC shows its progress and result.

### Improved
- SYNQ Desktop no longer opens a console window; logs go to a file instead.
- The SYNQ icon now shows in the taskbar, Start menu and Explorer.
- SYNQ Setup: license agreement, choice of install folder, smoother pages.
- A fresh install starts with the first-run setup; development builds keep
  their own settings and never mix with the installed app.
- Lighter: fewer redraws when SYNQ is in the background, smaller downloads.
- This release also tests automatic updates from 0.2.0.

### New
- Pairing required: every connection is a Noise IK handshake with a paired phone; unpaired phones get the pairing code automatically.
- Disconnect on the PC now stops the phone for good (authenticated kick).
- Now Playing: see and control what any app plays (Spotify, Chrome, Brave, Apple Music…) — seek, ±10 s, previous/next, shuffle, repeat — on the PC and the phone.
- New black-and-white design with onboarding on Windows and Android.
- Tray icon, minimize to tray, full screen (F11), two-column wide layout.
- SYNQ Setup installer and signed automatic updates.
